title: Quantum Mechanics
subject: Quantum
summary: Undergraduate quantum mechanics at Griffiths-Schroeter depth (wave mechanics, formalism, hydrogen, angular momentum and spin, identical particles, perturbation theory, variational and WKB methods, time-dependent theory, scattering) plus three grad-touch units from Sakurai on kets, pictures, rotations, Wigner-Eckart, symmetries, density matrices, and Bell's theorem. Chemistry hooks run throughout: orbitals, vibrations, spin and NMR, selection rules, variational MO theory.

units.title: The Wave Function and Statistical Interpretation
units.summary: Wave mechanics from scratch: the Schrödinger equation, Born's probabilistic reading of the wave function, expectation values, the momentum operator, and the Heisenberg uncertainty principle; the ideas behind every later chemistry-facing use of orbitals as probability amplitudes.

lessons.title: The Schrödinger equation and Born's statistical interpretation
objectives: State the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for one particle in a potential V(x,t) and identify each term (kinetic, potential, time derivative).
Explain Born's rule: |Psi(x,t)|^2 dx is the probability of finding the particle in dx, and say why the wave function itself must be complex.
Contrast the quantum description with a classical trajectory, and describe what a position measurement does to Psi (collapse) in the Copenhagen reading.
Compare the discrete-orbit picture from Bohr's atom with the probability-cloud picture of an orbital the chemist already uses.
